summary: Every manual rule (1.1-6.1) and both carve-outs left to today's code (edge-payday corrections and weeks under 1,000 cents) have fixtures that isolate them and change the outcome when the rule is wrong. Every expected figure I recomputed by hand from the manual agrees with the sealed value. Comparison is type-strict and ignores key order. The only issue is an Advisory false-rejection path: the read-probe control depends on the candidate-editable /app/README.md.

unread_or_truncated_ranges: tests/shipped/app/** not opened individually: packet-manifest.json lists SHA-256 values identical to the environment/app counterparts I read (e.g. tdbenefit_run.py 272fd415..., payroll.py 24af57c7...), so the content was reviewed through those files.

findings.claim: The read-probe control in test_candidate_cannot_read_verifier_state uses /app/README.md as its world-readable file. A candidate that deletes or moves the README, which the contract does not forbid, makes that control fail and turns the reward to 0 without any statement being wrong.

finding_evidence.expected_behavior: The instruction only fixes /app/tools/tdbenefit_run.py byte for byte (instruction.md:1). It asks for statements from the driver and places no requirement on README.md bytes or presence, so a submission with correct statements and an unchanged driver should earn reward 1.
finding_evidence.actual_behavior: If /app/README.md is missing, the probe's open() raises OSError and the probe exits 0. _unreadable_by_candidate then returns True, so `assert not _unreadable_by_candidate('/app/README.md')` fails.
finding_evidence.trace_or_receipt: test_outputs.py:450-453: the probe exits 0 on OSError, and a return code of 0 means 'unreadable'. test_outputs.py:460 asserts that README.md is readable, as a control. test.sh:16 applies chmod -R a+rX /app, which fixes permissions but cannot restore a deleted file. test.sh:20-26 sets reward 1 only when pytest returns 0.

findings.reachable_case_or_path: The candidate fixes src/tdbenefit correctly, leaves the driver untouched, and removes or renames /app/README.md (for example while restructuring docs). test_candidate_cannot_read_verifier_state fails, pytest returns non-zero and the reward is 0.
findings.graded_effect: A solution with correct statements can be rejected over a file the contract does not grade. The action is implausible for a normal solver, so I leave this outside the blocking decision.
findings.root_invariant: Verifier self-checks should depend only on state the verifier creates or the contract pins, not on candidate-editable files that are not graded.
sibling_variants: No other control reads candidate-editable files. The driver checks at test_outputs.py:463-469 rest on the contract-pinned driver path, and /tests, ROSTER, the shipped copy and /logs/verifier are all verifier-owned.
interaction_variants: test.sh:16 chmod -R a+rX /app handles permissions but not deletion or replacement with a directory. A README.md replaced by a directory is still readable through os.listdir in the probe, so only deletion or rename triggers the failure.
findings.minimal_repair_boundary: Make the control probe read a world-readable file the verifier creates itself (for example in a fresh 0755 tempdir), not /app/README.md.
closure_evidence: Delete /app/README.md in an otherwise-correct submission and confirm the reward stays 1.
Confirm that the control still fails when the probe user cannot read the verifier-created file.

checks_performed: Mapped every numbered manual rule (1.1-6.1) and both carve-outs left to today's code to a named test and fixture in test_outputs.py:243-342.

Recomputed sealed expectations by hand from the manual (not from any reference). Claims checked: W601086, W543087, W217093 (low_partial_weeks); W774079, W854080, W514085 (corrections); W950007 (weeks_pay); W104035, W834038 (rate_bounds); W214027, W735028, W358032 (row_in_force); W937042, W884039, W799040, W771041 (low_wage_rate); W783045 (399-day period); W784054 (14-day retro); W661070 (partial cap); W727076 (no wage loss); W297107, W369105, W189103 (limits); W100111 (generated); and the four hand-worked row-figure claims. Every recomputed value matched.

Traced the shipped package for each differential pair and job to confirm the pairs are contract-grounded. differential-corrections: the 1,999- and 777-cent edge lines keep the payday week. differential-low_partial_weeks: shipped and manual agree on AWW and rate (150,000/80,000 max-capped and 80,001/60,000 min-held); rows 3-4 separate 3/5 from 2/3.

Checked the plausible wrong implementations below against the fixtures and found each one fails: divide by weeks paid, 3/5 rate, newest row, row effective after the injury, missing 3.5 or <= in 3.5, 3.5 tested against the 2/3 figure, exclusive period days, 7 waiting days, retro at >14, floored ttd, uncapped partial, 3/5 or 2/3 applied to all partial weeks, zero benefit for low weeks, tpd_weeks counting only weeks of 1,000 cents or more, corrections shifted like a week's pay or dropped, negative wage loss, and weeks' pay not shifted.

Checked that compare() parses the JSON, compares keys as a set (not in order), compares values type-strictly (rejecting bool and float) and checks statement order. The instruction and README require these.

Checked the execution path: the driver is replaced by the verifier's copy, /app is sealed, then setpriv runs as the unprivileged uid with -I -S under the same pinned python 3.13 image as the environment, the job file has a neutral name and cwd is fresh. The stdlib-only package runs under -S.
Checked that within_limits enforces section 1 on every sealed job and on every relabelled or hand-worked job, and that trap_inputs confines inputs the manual leaves open to their declared families.

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails when it is missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: Each rule family compares complete statements type-strictly. Every rule has at least one fixture whose outcome changes when the rule is wrong, e.g. W854080 for corrections, W809008/W616009 for the 2,000-cent threshold, W358032 for row in force, W834038 for 3.5 compared against the 2/3 figure, and the 13/14/15 retro claims.

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result (values, membership, uniqueness, required outputs)
coverage_sweep.reason: compare() requires exactly one top-level key, the statement count, the exact key set, integer types and equal values for all ten fields.

coverage_sweep.category: Isolating case for each named domain rule (not only held-out variation)
coverage_sweep.reason: There is one family per rule, and the fixtures are built to isolate it: every weekday of injury, both base-period edges, 1/5/9/12-week divisors, rate at, above and below max and min, the day before, on and after a row change, one-day and 399-day periods, 1-4 waiting days, remainders in ttd rounding, and 999/1,000/1,001-cent weeks. Hand-worked row-figure jobs cover the 40th row and the extreme max and min figures.

coverage_sweep.category: Try plausible incorrect solutions and confirm rejection
coverage_sweep.reason: About 20 wrong variants traced statically (see checks_performed). Each fails on at least one sealed fixture. The 3/5 low-week share is separated from 2/3 by W601086/W543087 and by differential rows 3-4 (80,001 AWW, rate held at the 60,000 minimum). The low-week cap is shown by W217093 and differential rows 1-2.

coverage_sweep.category: Accept contract-valid alternatives (formatting, ordering, implementation choices)
coverage_sweep.reason: Output is parsed JSON with key order ignored, and the driver is fixed. The shuffled wage-line order, which the README permits, is exercised by relabel(). Claim names are drawn from the full 1-24 character domain, including spaces, quotes and non-ASCII. Guards that act only outside section 1 cannot change graded results. The one false-rejection path, a file outside the contract, is reported as AXIS-1.

coverage_sweep.category: Enforce documented restrictions (driver unchanged, carve-outs left to today's code)
coverage_sweep.reason: The delivered driver's bytes are recorded before replacement and compared with the shipped copy, which hash-matches the environment copy. test.sh re-checks the driver with cmp. Both carve-outs are enforced by sealed expectations plus differentials against the shipped package, and trap_inputs keeps other families free of those inputs.

coverage_sweep.category: Proxy behavior, Oracle-specific representation, stale binaries, self-controlled comparisons, unreachable cases
coverage_sweep.reason: The expectations are sealed and pinned by digest. The shipped comparison copy is verifier-owned (uid 65533, mode 0700). Every sealed job passes the section 1 check, so every graded case is reachable. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and -I -S are set. No comparison depends on candidate-controlled data.
There is no state machine. For the signed wage loss, earnings below the AWW, equal to it (47,662 vs 47,662) and above it (500,000) are all present, as is AWW 0 with earnings of 1,000 or more.

coverage_sweep.category: Semantic content vs native encoding/layout/diagnostic output
coverage_sweep.reason: The only representation promise, integer JSON values with the claim as a string, is enforced type-strictly. Bytes, key order and whitespace are not imposed. stderr is ignored except on failure.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: W809008: a 2,000-cent line on 2028-10-27 shifts into base week 10-22, and treated as a correction it would sit in week 10-29, outside the base period. W616009: a 2,000-cent line on 2021-04-09 shifts out of the base period.
W854080/W145081: an edge line after the base period is excluded. W595082: an edge line at the first base week is included. Differential pair 2 checks the first-week edge against the shipped package.

rules: low-week share at today's 3/5 with a cap at the rate
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Max-capped rate: 3/5 of the loss exceeds the rate, so the cap binds (W217093, differential rows 1-2). Rate held at the minimum: 3/5 applies uncapped (differential rows 3-4). Uncapped rate: W601086 and W543087.

rules: 3.5 low-wage rate against that row's minimum
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: W358032: AWW 58,286 is below the newest row's minimum of 60,000 but above the in-force minimum of 52,000, so the rate is 52,000. W735028 and W372030 have AWW below the in-force minimum.

rules: 3.5 rate = AWW and 5.1 partial on zero wage loss
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: W345021 has no wage lines and W440022 has only out-of-base lines. Both give AWW 0 and rate 0. A 1,000-cent partial week gives tpd 0, and retro days are paid at a rate of 0.
W784054 reaches 14 days from three periods (5+4+5). W515046 has 12 periods. W755044 has 4 one- or two-day periods totalling 5 days.
